reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (2/4)

refSet.reason: 칩셋 dungeon 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: ground tile texture (dark slate patches with purple crisscross lines)

answer.evidence: The image is a full 64x16 opaque seamless terrain tile. Column scan shows uniform lightness (L about 37) across rows 0-15 with no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or front face. It is a flat top-down ground texture of dark slate patches separated by purple lines. This is expected for terrain and has no standing-object structure.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine on paper: 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the dark tones lean blue rather than black. By eye the candidate is weaker than those numbers suggest. It shows as a thin band of dark zigzag or scale marks sitting on an empty slate field, not a full 4x3 patch with surface structure. The contrast between its tones is very low, so the marks read as one dark mass, and the pattern repeats mechanically. It has only 7 colours in total, against 80 for the grass, and it lacks the stone-by-stone shading and per-unit highlights of the paving. It would look thinner and flatter than either reference. With that doubt, I fail it.

surfaces.part: ground tile texture (dark slate with purple crack pattern)

answer.evidence: The tile is a fully opaque 64x16 ground texture: a uniform dark slate-blue with a purple crack/vein pattern. The column scan shows one run across rows 0-15 with constant lightness (L~37). There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, vertical face or silhouette change, so it is a flat seamless terrain tile and not a standing object. It reads as a flat top-down surface, which is normal for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate does not read as a 4x3-tile ground patch. The board shows a large uniform dark slate field with only a thin zigzag band of dark blue pixels near the bottom. If that field is the candidate, it is a flat fill far larger than 5x5, which contradicts the 0% near-flat figure. The measured 5 visible tones and 7 raw colours per tile are low next to the grass reference (26 raw colours) and the 7-tone paving. The band shows only about 3 lightness steps and none of the per-stone shading or tuft clusters of the references. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark_material_tone), and that is the one point in its favour. Even on the measured tone count alone it is no richer than the paving reference, and the picture shows a flat, sparse piece that does not cover the patch. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: ground tile (dark slate with purple crack pattern, full 64x16 swatch)

answer.evidence: The image is a flat, seamless terrain tile of dark slate patches separated by purple crack lines. The column scan shows uniform lightness (L about 37) over rows 0-15, and the width is a constant 64 across all rows. It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, and no front face. This is a flat top-down ground texture, which is what the terrain kind expects, so it is not a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: By eye, the candidate is a dark slate field with only a thin zigzag band of dark blue along the bottom. It does not read as a 4x3-tile ground patch like the grass or paving references. Most of the area is one flat colour with no grain, tufts, stones or tile variation, so the 0% near-flat figure does not match what I see. Only about 7 colours exist in total, against 80 in the grass reference. The 5 visible tones per tile probably come from the band, not from a textured surface. The paving reference shows 7 tones with individually shaded stones, and the candidate has no equivalent. Dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is not a black sticker line, but that does not offset the missing surface texture and shading depth. A careful artist would not accept this next to the references.

surfaces.part: ground tile (dark slate with purple crack pattern)

answer.evidence: The tile is a full 64x16 opaque ground texture with uniform lightness (L about 37) in every column. It shows dark slate patches separated by purple crack lines and no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical front face. It is a flat terrain fill and not a standing object, so it reads as a top-down surface texture.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate does not read as a 4x3-tile ground patch. Most of its area is a flat slate-blue field, and the only detail is a thin dark zigzag band of roughly 50x17 source pixels along the bottom. The zigzag is a repeated motif with little tonal variation, not grass tufts, soil grain or stones shaded one by one as in the Beodeul grass and paving references. I see about 4 usable lightness steps against 5-6 in the references. The measured facts are 5 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage, but the picture shows large uniform areas, so I treat the measured flat figure as unreliable here. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted blue-grey rather than near-black, which is fine. Overall it looks thinner and flatter than the references and does not fill the patch with texture the way they do.
